title: Linear accessibility of uncued candidate values
research_question: Does the block state permit less linear decoding of the three uncued candidate values at delay32 than the matched random state?
strongest_rejection_reason: Linear decoding tests coordinate/decoder accessibility, not total information or semantic hypothesis states.
hypothesis: Uncued candidate decoding difference M3-C0 <=-5pp with paired CI upper<-5pp at delay32, subject to adequacy and original-behavior guards.
intervention: Identical fixed ridge probe on frozen pre-evidence hidden states; no recurrent intervention
dataset: Fresh task-generator streams 850000/860000/870000+delay for probe train/validation/test
metrics: behavioral pre/final and common early-correct pair secondary
resource_matching: M3/C0 trained weights inherited from matched EXP-0004; identical 1040-coefficient ridge probe, state dimension, sample counts and inference steps
interpretation: Uncued candidate labels are near-linearly decodable in both models; the preregistered >=5pp block deficit is excluded, while original task behavior differs.
next_action: STOP_MECHANISM_ESCALATION; do not rescue architecture. A distinct fixed-probe cross-delay mapping question can be registered without changing model weights or Gate1.
